The rollout is concentric. Each survey day sits in its own distance band from the hospital — the crew worked outward, ring by ring, never doubling back.

Map layers

Localities covered

How this was built. 491 photos across three dated folders were OCR'd for their GPS Map Camera stamp; every one yielded a latitude, longitude and address. Repeat shots of one pole were merged (≤20 m apart, within 5 min) into 425 board sites. Roads, localities and land use are real OpenStreetMap geometry. One caveat: 17 boards on St Anns Church Rd share an identical frozen GPS fix — they stack on a single point and are drawn in violet.

Mounted in five zones, mostly not in HBR. 24 of the 30 autos were wrapped in the Kammanahalli–Lingarajapuram belt about 2–3 km south of the hospital; only 6 were done in HBR Layout itself.

Mounting zones

Where they are registered

RTO

Teal marks the two RTOs whose jurisdiction covers HBR Layout. Only 5 of 30 autos are registered there — an RTO code records where a vehicle was registered, not where it plies.

Vehicles

About these positions. The auto photos come from a different camera app than the pole-board survey: it stamps only a reverse-geocoded street address, no latitude/longitude. Each zone below is geocoded from that address against OpenStreetMap, so it is accurate to roughly a block — unlike the board sites, which carry exact coordinates. All 30 autos were photographed on 19 Aug 2026, 12:31 PM–5:11 PM.
